root_cause_criterion.criterion: When `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()` resumes from `CUR_CHAR(l)`, it must not execute `NEXTL(l)` if malformed-byte recovery has already halted the parser and set `ctxt->instate` to `XML_PARSER_EOF`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original returns from `CUR_CHAR(l)` with `ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF` after `xmlHaltParser()` rebound the input to the global empty-string sentinel, but still falls through to `NEXTL(l)`. The fixed original inserts the missing EOF guard at the same source site and returns before the protected advance.

nodes.state: `xmlHaltParser()` rebinds `ctxt->input->cur/base/end` to `BAD_CAST ""`, establishing the empty-string sentinel pointer later reused in the vulnerable attribute loop.
The vulnerable `NEXTL(l)` mutates `ctxt->input->cur` from the reset sentinel pointer to the next byte position, advancing `BAD_CAST ""` to `BAD_CAST "" + 1`.
The next `while ((CUR != 0) && (CUR != stop))` evaluation reuses the already-advanced cursor and dereferences `*ctxt->input->cur` at the one-byte-past-empty-string address.

edges.relation: The same cursor pointer rebound by `xmlHaltParser()` to the empty-string sentinel is the `ctxt->input->cur` seen immediately after `c = CUR_CHAR(l);` returns to `htmlParseHTMLAttribute()`.
The reset cursor value present after `CUR_CHAR(l)` is the same `ctxt->input->cur` consumed by the subsequent vulnerable `NEXTL(l)` call.
The exact cursor pointer produced by vulnerable `NEXTL(l)` is the pointer re-read at the next loop-header `CUR` evaluation that triggers the ASan sink.
